abstract:
Bovine coronavirus (BCoV) is a significant pathogen responsible for neonatal calf diarrhea and respiratory disorders. The spike (S) protein plays a pivotal role in mediating viral entry into host cells and eliciting immune responses. This study conducted a comprehensive analysis of the complete S gene sequences from field isolates.
Nested PCR screening of 236 fecal samples collected from nine leagues and cities in Inner Mongolia yielded a positive rate of 7.63% (18/236), with marked regional variation; notably, Hinggan (Xing'an) League accounted for the largest proportion of positive cases (38.89%, 7/18 of total positives). Four complete S gene sequences (4092 bp) were obtained from positive specimens. Phylogenetic analysis demonstrated that the Inner Mongolian strains clustered within the Genogroup II (GII) lineage. Comparative analysis of the S protein amino acid sequences identified seven variation sites. Bioinformatics prediction suggested that the variant strain may possess altered antigenic properties, although these computational predictions require experimental validation. While the transmembrane domain (1308-1328) and the signal peptide cleavage site were highly conserved, variations in glycosylation and phosphorylation sites were observed. The secondary structure was predominantly composed of random coils (51.65% - 52.24%), suggesting structural flexibility. Furthermore, key functional motifs were conserved, although mutations within the receptor-binding domain (RBD), such as G573E, were identified, which warrant further investigation to determine their functional implications.
This study provides a preliminary investigation into the epidemiology of BCoV in Inner Mongolia and analyzes the genetic variation of the S protein. These findings offer descriptive insights into the epidemiological patterns of BCoV in Inner Mongolia and establish a baseline for continuous molecular surveillance. While the identified genetic variations may provide reference information for future research, including vaccine-related studies, such implications remain speculative and would require extensive experimental validation.
